extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media scholars, First Amendment advocates, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and normative guidance for judging whether journalism serves the First Amendment's democratic functions—i.e., what kinds of reporting deserve constitutional protection and editorial prioritization. Useful for newsroom editors, media scholars, and advocates deciding what to cover and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional press function (distribution for self-government)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unique constitutional value served by the press is the distribution of information necessary for self-government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative touchstone: prioritize reporting that supplies citizens with facts needed to participate in democratic governance and public decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens need facts for self-governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News judged valuable when it conveys accurate, timely facts that enable informed civic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watchdog of government
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and report wrongdoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize investigative reporting that uncovers corruption, abuse, or misuse of power; supports accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum for public debate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an arena for discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create and sustain spaces for a range of viewpoints, debate, and deliberation on public matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education of voters
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform and educate the electorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage that explains policy choices, stakes, procedures, and implications to help voters make decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding power accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor government, business, and institutions to hold them accountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess stories by their capacity to reveal actions of institutions and actors that affect the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-majoritarian voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect minorities from tyranny by giving voice to those outside the majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include marginalized or minority perspectives that may be overlooked by majoritarian politics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government accountability (newsworthiness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of actions of elected officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories about officials' decisions, conduct, and oversight are democratically valuable because they enable public scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy implications
rubrics_metrics.description: What government decisions mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on the consequences and trade-offs of policies for citizens, not just the policies themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting / electoral information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about voting processes and elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes voter education, election mechanics, candidate positions, and integrity of electoral systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrongdoing exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposure of corruption, fraud, abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative and reporting efforts that uncover illicit or unethical conduct are high democratic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public spending
rubrics_metrics.description: How tax dollars and public funds are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of budgets, spending decisions, and procurement that affect public resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on the judicial branch and significant rulings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain legal outcomes and their broader societal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency and regulatory decisions affecting citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track rulemaking, enforcement, and the administrative state where it impacts rights or daily life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public health and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about threats to health and safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely, accurate reporting on public health risks and safety issues serves democratic necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil rights and liberties
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of rights, liberties, and their protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight threats to constitutional and civil rights and how they are defended or eroded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues affecting the fairness and reliability of elections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate and explain fraud claims, administration problems, and reforms that affect trust in results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissenting voices
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that amplifies opposition and minority viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include perspectives that challenge prevailing power or majoritarian narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about different policy options and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help the public weigh alternatives, not just report on dominant proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: International affairs affecting nation
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign events with domestic significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize international reporting when it has clear implications for national policy, security, or citizens' lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage of macro- and microeconomic trends and impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain economic indicators, employment, markets, and how they affect public welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality and access
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on disparities and access to resources or services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight structural inequalities and barriers to opportunity or services that undermine democratic participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: What's less democratically valuable (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics judged lower priority for democratic function: pure entertainment/celebrity, lifestyle/consumer, sports, sensationalized crime, tabloid scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topics generally have limited First Amendment democratic value and should not displace coverage crucial to self-government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage tensions between competing values
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and balance tensions such as public service vs. public interest (what people want vs. what they need); free press vs. profit motive; watchdog role vs. economic dependence; editorial judgment vs. algorithmic delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisionmaking should explicitly weigh these trade-offs and seek to preserve democratic functions even when commercial incentives push otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-press legal precedents defining function
rubrics_metrics.description: Key cases that shape constitutional protections and press function: New York Times v. Sullivan (1964) — actual malice standard; Pentagon Papers (1971) — prior restraint limits; Branzburg v. Hayes (1972) — reporter's privilege debated; New York Times v. United States (1971) — government secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge of these precedents is part of assessing what press activity receives strong constitutional protection and how courts weigh press interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-government enabling (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: News should enable self-government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core normative criterion emphasizing information that supports citizens' capacity to govern themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watchdog producing (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press should produce watchdog reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative emphasis on investigations and reporting that expose wrongdoing and hold power to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forum-creating (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press should create forums for public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support platforms and practices that allow diverse civic discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from power (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain editorial and institutional independence from governmental or private power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess structures and funding sources that might compromise independence; favor independent reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality of voice (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure a plurality of viewpoints in the public sphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage should represent diverse social, political, and cultural perspectives to avoid dominance by a single voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-majoritarian protection (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect minority voices against majoritarian suppression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value stories that amplify marginalized groups or challenge dominant majoritarian decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth pursuing (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to seeking and reporting the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accuracy, fact-checking, and correction practices are central measures of democratic journalistic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interest serving (First Amendment tradition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Serve the public interest in editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize reporting that addresses community needs and collective welfare over purely commercial concerns.
